name: 4dgl-intellisense
description: Open-source, community-built IDE support for 4D Systems 4DGL (hover docs, completion, signature help, semantic highlighting, and syntax/name/argument diagnostics). Not affiliated with 4D Systems. Supports function types but not libraries; #include targets must live within the project directory to resolve — it does not ship the full 4D Systems include folder.

4dgl.library.description: The 4D Systems internal functions library to use for hover docs, completion, and signature help. Leave unset to be prompted on first use.

4dgl.diagnostics.enabled.description: Highlight 4DGL syntax errors in the editor. Reports block-structure and delimiter problems only (unclosed func/if/while, mismatched block terminators, unbalanced brackets, unterminated strings and comments) — it does not resolve names or evaluate pre-processor conditions.

4dgl.diagnostics.unknownDirectives.description: Warn about a pre-processor directive that isn't documented in the 4DGL reference. Directives your file redefines with `#constant #alias $#REAL` are recognised. Turn this off if your project uses a directive the reference doesn't list.

4dgl.diagnostics.assignmentOperator.description: Warn about a bare `=`, which is not a 4DGL operator — assignment is `:=` and comparison is `==`.

4dgl.diagnostics.unknownFunctions.description: Warn when a call looks like a misspelling of a known function (including a wrong-case one - 4DGL is case sensitive). Only near-misses are reported: a name resembling nothing known is left alone, because it may come from an #inherit target outside the workspace, or be one of the shortcut functions the manuals only mention in prose.

4dgl.diagnostics.unknownConstants.description: Warn when an ALL_CAPS reference looks like a misspelling of a known constant. Same near-miss rule as 4dgl.diagnostics.unknownFunctions. Lower-case and mixed-case names are never reported, since they can't be told apart from variables.

4dgl.diagnostics.argumentCount.description: Warn when a call passes the wrong number of arguments. Exact for your own functions. For built-ins the count comes from the documented signature, and the ~2% of functions whose signature the manuals' own examples contradict are skipped rather than guessed at. Calls using the @ argument-pointer operator are never checked.

4dgl.diagnostics.knownNames.description: Extra names to treat as defined, so they are never reported as unknown. Useful for symbols from an #inherit target outside the workspace, or a constant the 4DGL manuals don't document.
